masking: phantom and control names are pseudonyms from phantomdeps.util.mask_key(eco, None, name), which normalises the name as the registry compares it (PEP 503 for PyPI, lower-case elsewhere) so each equals the paper's per-declaration pseudonym in data/runs/*/deps_masked.jsonl; stdout/stderr tails are omitted; the file is verified to contain no real name
notes: All registries listen on 127.0.0.1 only; no package is published to any real registry.

With --netns (as for the recorded run) the whole replay runs in a fresh network namespace whose only interface is loopback (network_isolation, read from /proc/self/net before any server starts), so no installer or build step can reach anything but the local registries, whatever it tries.
Packages are harmless: they only write the fixed marker text to $REPLAY_MARKER_DIR.

P1 = installer default (resolves-now). P3 here = the installers' own as-of-h date filters (uv --exclude-newer, npm --before); pip, cargo and the ESP-IDF component manager have no such option (recorded not_available). The paper's P3 is the record-age policy, which these filters match only when a name's earliest artifact dates its record (PROTOCOL.md, section 7).

SCII pipeline ORDER: decide the gate items (res, est) first from what the registry reports; run the pin lock step ONLY if the gate passes (G==1); then decide with the measured pin; then install only on admit. A squat (G==0 or None) never reaches the lock step, so no unvetted package code is run to collect evidence.

Pin evidence is CODE-FREE: npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts (integrity); cargo generate-lockfile (checksum); uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-build (sha256). The controls are published as an inert wheel + sdist so --no-build reads the wheel without building; squats are sdist-only. marker_after_lock is recorded for every lock step (false throughout). scii.no_pin keeps the pin=None decision for comparison.

Resolving an sdist-only package with uv WITHOUT --no-build runs its build backend (get_requires_for_build_wheel / prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel) -- package-authored code. The top-level lock_execution section measures this directly on each squat with a distinct metadata-hook marker (code_ran_during_lock), which is exactly why the gate runs before any lock step and the pin comes from code-free locking.

Bound models: npm time.created and crates pubtime bound the record from both sides; PyPI upload times bound it only from above (tau_lo=None on first contact) unless a real pre-publish absence lookup supplies tau_lo (the 'with_absence' variant).
cargo has no stable publication-date install filter, so P3 is not available for crates.

Controls are NOT pre-existing packages: they are published DURING the replay with a record date the harness set control_backdate_days (180) before the horizon (record_date_set_by_harness=true). They are not 'published before the horizon'.

dateless_control (PyPI): such a control served from an HTML-only index with no PEP 700 upload-time; the date filter stops it, first contact yields 'request', and one lookup of the record date at the PEP 691 origin index answers the request so the build can complete.

Ordering is made real per squat and asserted (ordering_check): absence lookup first, then build+publish (the registry stamps the publish instant), so absence_time < publication_time; t_gate is taken after an ecosystem's squats are published, so publication_time <= t_gate and P2 age >= 0.

espidf (CPS stand-in): the REAL idf-component-manager 3.1.2 resolves+downloads one harmless marker component from a local static-storage mock on 127.0.0.1 (GET /components/<ns>/<name>.json, then the .tgz and CHECKSUMS.json), driven via its download_project_dependencies/version-solver API. P1 ('resolves now') admits the squat: its payload is unpacked into managed_components/ and the packed marker file is MATERIALISED into the build tree (marker=1). Unlike pip/npm/cargo, downloading a component runs NO component code: the component's CMake file writes a second marker when it is evaluated, and it is absent after the download (P1_download_code_ran=0).

espidf build: the REAL ESP-IDF build system (esp_idf in tool_versions; a shallow release checkout without git submodules, IDF_SKIP_CHECK_SUBMODULES=1) runs 'idf.py --preview build' for the linux host target (host gcc, no cross toolchain) on a minimal application whose main/idf_component.yml declares the component. The build calls the component manager at configure time, which downloads the component from the mock; CMake evaluates its CMakeLists.txt (cmake_marker: component code ran during the build) and compiles its source into the component library (component_lib). Under P1 the squat is built; under SCII the squat is rejected before any download or build, and the admitted control is built from the lock file the gate measured (pin_matches_build: the hash in the build's lock equals the measured pin). The application is not flashed or run.

espidf is REC_LOWER+REC_UPPER (like crates): the component record date (created_at) bounds the gate from both sides. The squat's record date is stamped at publish (after h), so est is refuted (G=0) and the SCII gate REJECTS it at first contact and with-absence, never reaching the lock step or installer. The backdated control (record date control_backdate_days before h) is established (est=1) and admitted.

espidf pin is CODE-FREE: the version solver + lock-file dump (no download, no unpack) records the component_hash the static storage serves; the lock step creates no managed_components and runs no component code (code_ran_during_lock=0). idf-component-manager has no publication-date install filter, so P3 is not available for espidf (like cargo).

The espidf scenario with role 'squat' is a stand-in, not a squat (the paper says so): every ESP-IDF phantom of the pilot's greedy pass lies in Espressif's own namespace, which no outsider can publish into. Its name is a classified ESP phantom's keyed pseudonym (mask_key('espidf', owner, name), which embeds the namespace), used verbatim as the operational component name under a placeholder local namespace. It is a harmless ph-<hex> placeholder that never resolves on the real registry, and mask_key is idempotent on it, so it equals the paper's per-declaration pseudonym and cross-checks.
